scope: Prepare the existing exact river-span spatial index before dense terrain/scatter batch sampling.
status: Exact numerical/transport equivalence and new packaged worker/native loading checks passed. Not a rendering-hitch fix.
finding: The regular terrain grid and scatter projections scanned whole nearby river reaches. Channel refinement prepared the same patch's spatial index only after the regular-grid work had finished.
change: Prepare once at the batch entry, including bounded subpatches of far terrain. Actual river algorithms, span order, kernel, water datum, sampling spacing and index bounds remain unchanged.
main_thread: One-off walking/player patches keep their existing lazy path; no automatic index setup was added to arbitrary samples.

proof.method: All serialized terrain, water, flora and placement fields must match the unchanged packaged worker; normalize only the measured mesh build-duration field.

component_observations.conditions: One instrumented CoreCLR100m/64segment tile at the same glacial valley coordinate; full output equivalence separately checked.
component_observations.limits: Component observations, not whole-game FPS or proof of all loading times. New packaged worker/native scene still required.

native.note: The previous same-scene candidate failed its 300-second coverage gate. Indexed candidate completed the gate with 428 tiles. Moving test still has frame spikes; this demonstrates loading/component benefit only.

costs: A temporary finite index per worker batch; no new global world layer, scenery, tick, shader sample, density reduction or draw call. Existing working-set lifetime remains batch-owned.
